core_obligations: Assume (1) and take an element m whose annihilator I has p minimal over it; since localisation is exact the annihilator localises to I_p, so pR_p is minimal over the annihilator of m in the localisation, which gives both (2) and (3) (proof lines 16179-16186).
(2) implies (3) by applying the first implication to the localised module over the localised ring (proof lines 16189-16190).

Assume (3): an element m/f whose annihilator has radical pR_p gives an element m of M whose annihilator I has radical localising to pR_p, so p contains I and is minimal over it, which is (1) (proof lines 16192-16199).
proof_roadmap: Turn the first condition into the localised statement through exactness of localisation (proof lines 16178-16186).
Close the cycle of implications back to the first condition (proof lines 16188-16200).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a prime p of a ring R and an R-module M, three conditions are equivalent: p is weakly associated to M, pR_p is weakly associated to M_p, and M_p has an element whose annihilator has radical pR_p (statement lines 16164-16176). The proof does not compute with primary decomposition: it unwinds the first condition into minimality of p over the annihilator of an element, uses exactness of localisation to transport that annihilator, and then closes the cycle of implications by a radical computation on the localised annihilator (proof lines 16178-16200). The middle step, which reuses the first implication on the localised module, is what keeps the argument short, and the author writes each implication out. H2.
